knowledge_abstraction.bug_theme: Normalization over fully masked or non-finite reduction slices
knowledge_abstraction.general_principle: Reduction-normalization operations may assume at least one finite value in each reduction slice; when all values are masked to -inf, the max-subtraction and normalization denominator can become numerically invalid and produce NaN instead of a safe fallback.

risk_dimensions.shape: Reduction slices where all positions are masked out; zero effective valid length along the reduction dimension
risk_dimensions.dtype: Floating-point dtypes that support -inf and NaN, such as float32, float16, and bfloat16
risk_dimensions.device: Different backends may implement masked softmax fallback inconsistently
risk_dimensions.execution_state: Operation is applied to tensors containing one or more fully non-finite reduction slices

failure_mechanism.description: Softmax-style normalization computes exp(value - max) and divides by the sum of those exponentials. When a reduction slice contains only -inf, the adjusted values and normalization denominator become invalid, causing NaN outputs rather than a defined zero-probability fallback.

input_exploration: Generate tensors with entire reduction slices set to -inf
Mix fully non-finite slices with finite slices along the same reduction dimension
Introduce inf, -inf, and NaN values into reduction inputs
Vary floating-point dtypes and reduction dimensions
constraint_awareness: Softmax-style kernels may assume every reduction slice contains at least one finite value
Attention-like masks can produce fully masked rows before normalization
Safe implementations often need explicit handling for empty or fully masked slices
oracle_strategy: Detect NaN outputs with torch.isnan or equivalent
Compare fully non-finite slices against a safe fallback such as zero probability vectors
Check output invariants such as finite probabilities and row-wise sums equal to one

transferability.reason: Any normalization or masked reduction over scores or weights can encounter fully invalid reduction slices, including log_softmax, attention weight computation, and masked loss reductions, so the principle generalizes beyond torch.softmax.

important_considerations: Target normalization and masked reduction APIs that consume score-like or weight-like inputs
Explore fully masked or fully non-finite reduction slices under different dtypes and devices
Verify fallback behavior when no finite value exists in a reduction slice
generation_strategy: Construct varied tensors where some reduction slices contain only -inf, inf, or NaN values
Apply masks that remove all valid positions for selected rows before normalization
Use invariant checks and safe fallback references to detect NaN or incorrect outputs
